advisory.summary: FR-010/FR-023: an entry reached only through a symlink to a file outside the catalogue records the symlink path, not the regular-file target, so `git show <ref>:<path>` returns the link text instead of the hashed content.
advisory.fix: When a catalogued or merged path is a symlink, record the `_resolve_symlink` target as the entry path and the link as an alias, even when the target is not itself indexed; add a scratch-repo test with `CLAUDE.md -> docs/x.md`.

advisory.summary: ENG-24: glob_regex turns globs from the repository's `.factory/config.json` into backtracking regexes matched against every tracked path; a short pathological glob can stall instructions-record at every preflight (git calls have no timeout).
advisory.fix: Collapse consecutive wildcards and reject globs above a wildcard/length limit with an 'instructions config ignored' note, or use a segment-wise non-backtracking matcher; add a time-bounded test with a pathological glob.

advisory.summary: ENG-24: blob reads have no per-file or total size cap, and merge-time reads start one git process per uncached blob, so a config `include: ["**"]` or a huge tracked agent file is read fully into memory.
advisory.fix: Get sizes with `cat-file --batch-check`/`ls-tree -l`, skip entries above a per-file cap with a note, cap the total read through config matches, and batch merge-time reads.

advisory.summary: ENG-25: documented build/test commands now come from every root-scope entry, including ADRs, link-sourced and config `reference` entries. That widens which repository text becomes executed commands. FR-024 requires this, so the risk sits in the spec, not in a deviation.
advisory.fix: Consider limiting command sourcing to root-scope `always` entries (exclude `link`/`reference` kinds and ADRs), or require setup-commands confirmation when a command comes from anything other than a root catalogue agent file; amend FR-024 if adopted.

advisory.summary: FR-024: under cruise, a same-tier conflict between documented commands is settled 'first in index order', but no step records that choice with the setup-commands decision.
advisory.fix: State in step 5 that under cruise the same-tier conflict choice is recorded with `decisions-add grill setup-commands '<commands recorded>' --cruise-override` whether or not the detector proposed anything; extend the S6 contract test.

advisory.summary: ENG-6: new helpers `_git`, `ScanError`, `_resolve_symlink`, `_title` and `_entry_json` have no `New:` reason line in any commit body.
advisory.fix: Record the reasons in the next fix commit body or the PR text; consider dropping `_entry_json`, since the index is already serialised with sort_keys=True.

advisory.summary: ENG-17: a worktree re-record with unchanged index content still rewrites state.json (summary `ref` moves to the new HEAD) but commits nothing, leaving the run worktree dirty.
advisory.fix: Skip the `ref` update when content is unchanged, or commit state.json whenever it differs; assert a clean `git status` in the unchanged-record test.

advisory.summary: ENG-17 / F2.4 / FR-022: a previous index that is valid JSON but not an object (e.g. `[]`) raises TypeError in `{**previous, ...}`/`_index_delta` instead of producing a null delta and an 'unreadable' note.
advisory.fix: After loading, treat a non-dict (or entries missing path/hash/kind/scope) as unreadable: add the 'previous index unreadable' note and set previous = None; add a test with `[]`.

advisory.summary: FR-017: adoption is detected by `"-adopt-" in path.name`, so a repository whose name contains `-adopt-` scans a new run's pending file at the wrong ref (ending in a scan error).
advisory.fix: Detect an adoption pending run from its content (`branch` plus `spec_dir`) rather than from the file name.

advisory.summary: ENG-25: a `--ref` value reaches `git rev-parse` with no `--end-of-options`; the `^{commit}` suffix makes exploitation unlikely.
advisory.fix: Reject a ref starting with '-' with ScanError, or insert `--end-of-options` before the revision.

Under engineering.md 'Behaviour-changing', a change limited to configuration does not trigger ENG-1/ENG-2, so the commit needs no Red proof and its non-conforming Red text is not a defect. The user requested it at verify, and verify is green.
